IS: 6806 -197$ 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
SNOWGAUGE 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution 
on 31 January 1973, after the draft finalized by the Meteorological 
Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved ty the Mechanical 
Engineering Division Council. 

0,2 Accuracy in the measurement ol snowfall is of great importance 
in irrigation, flood control, power ge deration and in conservation of water 
resources. The Director General of Observatories, New Delhi, has been 
designated the sole authority for msuring the correct registration of 
precipitation in India and the In ia Meteorological Department is at 
present responsible for the testing an 1 certification of all types of precipita- 
tion gauges and rain measures made within the country. 

0.3 Specifications for various type of precipitation gauges in use at 
meteorological and other observatori ;s in the country have been prepared 
by the India Meteorological Department. Based on these specifications, 
the following Indian Standards have already been published: 

IS : 4849- 1968 Specification for rain measures 

IS : 5225-1969 Specification for raingauge, non-recording 

IS : 5235-1969 Specification for raingauge, recording 

This Indian Standard has, therefore, been prepared in the interest of the 
standardization of various N types of precipitation gauges and the accuracy 
of measurement of precipitation in different forms. 

0.4 In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given 
to the requirements laid down by the World Meteorological Organization, 
Geneva, in addition to the special requirements obtaining in this country. 

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



•Rules for rounding off numerical values (reuiud). 

% 



tS: 6806 -1974 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifics the requirements for 500 cm 2 snowgauge with 
wind shield, and the measure glasses to be used with it. 

2. DESCRIPTION 

2*1 The snowgauge consists of a 60 cm deep collector having an area of 
500 cm* mounted inside an Alter pattern wind shield one metre in 
diameter. . The gauge with its shield is installed on stand pipe support so 
that the orifice of the collector is at a height of 1'5 m above the ground 
when installed on a concrete platform rising 10 cm from ground level. 
Solid precipitation collected in the gauge is melted and the precipitation 
in millimetres is measured using the measure glasses conforming to the 
requirements given in Appendix A. 

3. MATERIAL 

3.1 The collector shall be made of a suitable material having the following 
properties: 

a) Rigidity end strength with no distortion or other deterioration 
when exposed to widely varying climatic conditions in the open 
air, while at the same time being light in weight; 

b) Freedom from attack by animal, insect or fungoid life; 

c) Smooth and permanent surface finish so as to facilitate free flow of 
precipitation; and 

d) Low thermal conductivity so as to minimize evaporation losses or 
condensation gains. 

3.1.1 While any material satisfying the above requirements may be used 
fibre glass reinforced polyester is considered as a suitable material. The 
material selected for the fabrication of the collector shall be such that it is 
capable of withstanding the weathering effects of exposure in the open for 
a period of not less than 15 years. 

3.2 The material for the rim of the collector shall be gun metal or 
aluminium alloy conforming to Grade A9 of IS : 617-1959*. 

3 .3 The ring for the wind shield and the connector for the ring shall be of 
stainless steel. 

3.4 The supporting columns shall be cast from aluminium and anodized. 

3.5 All other components shall be of anodized aluminium or similar 
material fully protected against the effects of exposure in the open for 
prolonged periods extending for a number of years. 



•Specification for aluminium and aluminium alloy ingots and castings for general 
engineering purposes. 



IS: 6806 -1973 

3.6 The nuts, bolts and washers shall be of galvanized iron fully protected 

against rusting and corrosion. 

4. DIMENSIONS 

4.1 The dimensions for the snowgauge and shield shall be as given in 

Fig. 1. 

4.1.1 The inside diameter of the collector rim shall be correct within 
± 0*5 mm of the specified value of 252*2 mm when measured in any four 
directions and the mean of the four values shall be within ±0*2 mm of the 
specified value. 

5. DESIGNATION 

5.1 For the purposes of inquiry or order, the snowgauge shall be designat- 
ed by the nominal area of the collector. 

Example: 

A complete snowgauge with wind shield conforming to this 
standard shall be designated as "Snowgauge 500 cm 2 
IS: 6806 *\ 

6. GENERAL REQjLJIREMENTS 

6.1 Collector — The collector shall be a cylindrical canister with a rim 
cemented firmly at the top. The rim, having a knife edge, shall be truly 
circular. The inner surface of the rim and the inside vertical wall of the 
canister shall be in one plane. The entire inner and outer surfaces of the 
collector shall have a smooth and permanent finish. Seams, if any, shall be 
of adequate strength and be water-tight. The bottom of the collector, if 
made of metal, shall be folded, brazed and sealed water-tight, 

6.1.1 The collector, if made of metal, shall be highly polished and 
lacquered; if made from glass fibre reinforced polyester, shall have a glossy 
finish, coloured light green or cream and have a nominal thickness of at 

least 2*5 mm. 

6.2 Supporting Columns and Wind Shield 

6.2.1 The collector shall rest over two cylindrical supporting columns 
provided with flanges. The two supporting columns shall be fitted to each 
other with bolts, nuts and washers. 

6.2.2 The top and bottom surfaces of the flanges of the columns shall be 
at right angles to the longitudinal axis. The mounting of the columns shall 
be such that the rim of the collector when mounted is truly horizontal.

IS: 6806 -1973 

6.2.3 The flanged socket shall be capable of receiving the collector easily 
such that when assembled the rim of the collector is truly horizontal. 

6.2.4 The support frame of the wind shield shall be made of four 
aluminium T pieces of 40 X 40 X 6 section fitted over the flanged socket at 
right angles to one another. It shall be fitted to the socket by nuts and 
bolts, such that it may be easily dismantled for packing. 

6.2.5 When completely assembled, the orifice of the collector shall be 
1 *4 metres from the bottom of the lower column and in the same plane as 
the top of the aluminium tapers. 

6.2.6 The ring of the shield shall be of stainless steel and shall have a 
diameter of approximately one metre. The tw r o ends of the ring shall be 
joined by means of a stainless steel connector. 

6.2*7 The tapers of the shield shall be made of aluminium and they shall 
be 32 in number. They shall hang freely and be capable of swinging in 
gentle breeze, when assembled on the stainless steel supporting ring. The 
individual tapers shall be spaced evenly over the ring by means of 28 long 
and 8 short aluminium spacers. 

7. MARKING 

7.1 Each snowgauge shall bear the following inscription engraved legibly 
and neatly on a brass name plate which shall be cemented firmly on the 
collector: 

a) The inscription ' SNOWGAUGE, 500 cm 2 '; 

b) Maker's name or recognized trade-mark; and 

c) Serial number and year of manufacture, for example, No. 123/ 
1972. 

7.1.1 Snowgauges may also be marked with the ISI Certification Mark 
on the rim or the body of the collector. 

Note — The use of the ISI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations 
made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that 
standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which 
is devised and supervised by ISI and operated by the producer. ISI marked 
products are also continuously checked by ISI for conformity to that standard as a 
further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the ISI 
Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained 
from the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. PACKING 

8.1 The collector shall be wrapped in tissue paper and packed carefully in 
a strong cardboard carton. All other parts shall be dismantled, and 



IS 1 6806- 1973 

wrapped in corrugutcd packing paper and packed in a wooden box along 
with the carton containing the collector. The packing shall be such that 
the collector and the other parts shall safely withstand normal transit risks. 
Alternatively, the instrument shall be packed as agreed to between the 
supplier and the purchaser. 

9. TESTING AND INSPECTION 

9.1 All the snowgauges shall be tested individually for conformity to all 
the requirements of this specification. 



APPENDIX A 

( Clause 2.1 ) 

REQUIREMENTS OF MEASURE GLASSES FOR 
SNOWGAUGE, 500 cm 2 

A-l. TERMINOLOGY 

A-l.l For the purpose of this appendix, the definitions given in IS : 1382- 
1961* shall apply. 

A-2. TYPES 

A-2.1 The measure glasses shall be of the following two types suitable for 
use with a collector of 500 cm 2 : 

a) 10 mm capacity ( Fig. 2 ), and 

b) 20 mm capacity ( Fig. 3 ). 

A«3. DESIGNATION 

A-3.1 For the purposes of inquiry or order, the measure glasses shall be 
designated by their maximum capacities. 



Example: 

* Measure Glass for Snowgauge, 500 cm 2 , 10 mm Capacity, 
IS : 6806 \ 

A-4. REQUIREMENTS 

A-4.1 The measure glasses shall meet the requirements given in IS : 4849- 
1968t for the material, limit of alkalinity, general construction and finish. 



•Glossary of terms relating to glass industry. 
{Specification for rain measures. 



IS 1 6806 • 1973 

A-5. DIMENSIONS 

A-5.1 The dimensions of the measure glasses shall be as given in Fig. 2 
and 3.

A-6. GRADUATION AND FIGURING 

A-6.1 The measure glasses shall meet the requirements laid down in 
IS: 4849-1968* for graduation and figuring except for the following 
deviations. 



•Specification for rain measures. 



IS 1 6606 -1973 

A~6.1.1 Graduations shall be engraved for every 0"1 mm as shown in 
Fig. 2 for (he measure glass having capacity oflO mm and for every 0*2 mm 
as shown in Fig. 3 for that having capacity of 20 mm. 

A-6.1.2 Every full mm graduation line shall be plainly figured by 
numbers not less than 5 mm high immediately opposite the end of the 
graduation line as shown in Fig. 2 and 3. Alternatively, the figures shall 
be placed immediately above the extended line to which they refer, 

A-7. BASIS OF CALIBRATION 

A-7,1 The measure glass of 10 mm capacity shall contain 500 cm 3 or 
49803 g of distilled water corresponding to 10 mm of rainfall when filled to 
its highest graduation mark, at a temperature of 27°C, 65 percent relative 
humidity and a pressure of 760 mm Hg. The lower edge of the water 
meniscus shall be in the horizontal plane containing the graduation marks. 
Similarly, the measure glass of 20 mm capacity shall contain 1 000 cm 8 or 
996*06 g of distilled water when filled to the highest graduation mark under 
the same conditions. 

A-8. TOLERANCES 

A-8.1 The maximum permissible error at any point as also the maximum 
permissible difference between errors at any two points not less than 
10 subdivisions removed from one another shall be ± 0*05 mm of snowfall 
in the measure glass having capacity of 10 mm while it shall be ± 0*1 mm for 
the measure glass having capacity of 20 mm. For testing and when using 
the measure glass the scale reading shall correspond to the position of the 
lower edge of the water meniscus. 

A-9. MARKING 

A-9.1 The measure glasses shall bear the following inscriptions engraved 
legibly: 

a) The mark * 10 mm ' or * 20 mm ' as the case may be, above the 
scale between the highest graduation mark and the top of the 
measure glass; 

b) The inscription c Measure glass for snowgauge, 500 cm 2 • engraved 
to the left of the scale; 

c) The maker's name or his recognized trade-mark; and 

d) Serial number and year of manufacture, for example, 'No. 123/ 
1972 \ 

10 



IS 1 6806- 1973 

A-lO. PACKING 

A-10.1 Each measure glass shall be packed in a cardboard carton suitably 
cushioned as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 

A-ll. SAMPLING AND INSPECTION 

A-U.l Representative samples shall be drawn and adjudged for conformity 
to this standard as prescribed in IS : 4426-1967*.
